Hi! I’m a B.Tech Cybersecurity student interested in space exploration, technology, and creative problem-solving. Our team has chosen “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” focusing on storytelling about NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.

I’m looking for teammates interested in programming, web development, UI/UX design, data visualization, research, and space science. Let’s work together to turn space history into an engaging and meaningful experience!
summary:
**Left Behind: Stories from the Moon and Mars**

Left Behind is an interactive web-based storytelling platform that brings the history of NASA's abandoned and inactive space hardware to life. We developed an interactive map featuring important mission sites on the Moon and Mars, including Apollo 11, Apollo 15, Viking 1, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.

Users can explore different locations, discover what equipment was left behind, understand why it was left there, and learn about its current status. Each location includes a first-person story told from the perspective of the hardware itself. The platform also includes a voice narration feature and an automated storytelling tour to make learning more engaging.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming NASA's space mission history into an interactive and educational experience. It is important because these machines are more than abandoned equipment; they represent human curiosity, scientific achievements, and milestones  space exploration.
details:
Project Details – Left Behind: Stories from the Moon and Mars

Left Behind: Stories from the Moon and Mars is an interactive educational website that explores NASA hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars after space missions. It helps users discover the history and importance of these objects through an engaging storytelling experience.

The website features interactive Moon and Mars maps with clickable markers representing mission locations, including Apollo 11, Apollo 15, Viking 1, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. When users select a location, they can explore information about the mission, the hardware left behind, why it remained there, and its current status. Each object is presented through a first-person storytelling approach, making the experience more interesting and understandable. The website also includes voice narration using the browser's Web Speech API, a guided tour, and navigation between locations.

The main benefit of this project is that it transforms space mission information into an interactive learning experience. It is designed especially for school students and space enthusiasts, helping them understand that space exploration leaves behind important scientific and historical evidence.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG for the interactive maps and website interface. The Web Speech API is used for voice narration, and Netlify is used for hosting and deployment.

The creative aspect of our project is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting only facts and timelines, we allow users to explore the stories of abandoned space hardware as if the objects themselves are speaking. We considered ease of use, educational value, accessibility, simple navigation, and engagement while designing the website.

Our intended impact is to create curiosity about space exploration, improve awareness of NASA's past missions, and encourage students to learn more about the history and legacy of human exploration beyond Earth.
